facts.statement: The type specimen for Leyesaurus is a nearly complete skull with an articulated jaw and some postcranial bones, including the spine and limb girdles.
facts.quote: Leyesaurus is known from the holotype PVSJ 706, a nearly complete skull with articulated mandible and some postcranial remains (vertebral column, scapular and pelvic girdles and hindlimb).

facts.statement: Leyesaurus had a skull measuring 18 centimeters long and an estimated total body length of 2.5 meters.
facts.quote: The skull has a length of 18 centimeters, and Leyesaurus has been estimated to have been about 2.5 m in length.

facts.statement: Leyesaurus fossils were found in the Quebrada del Barro Formation, which dates to the Lower Jurassic period.
facts.quote: It was collected from the uppermost part of the Quebrada del Barro Formation of the Marayes-El Carrizal Basin, dating to the Lower Jurassic

facts.statement: The dinosaur was discovered near the locality of Balde de Leyes in the Caucete Department of San Juan Province.
facts.quote: Leyesaurus was found near the locality Balde de Leyes, in the Caucete Department of San Juan Province.

facts.statement: Leyesaurus was first named by Cecilia Apaldetti, Ricardo N. Martinez, Oscar A. Alcober, and Diego Pol in 2011.
facts.quote: Leyesaurus was first named by Cecilia Apaldetti, Ricardo N. Martinez, Oscar A. Alcober and Diego Pol in 2011

facts.statement: The genus name honors the Leyes family, who lived in Balde de Leyes and discovered the holotype fossil.
facts.quote: The generic name honors the Leyes family, inhabitants of the small town Balde de Leyes, who discovered the holotype and notified the paleontologists of the San Juan Museum

facts.statement: The species name marayensis refers to the Marayes-El Carrizal Basin where the holotype was found.
facts.quote: The specific name refers to the Marayes-El Carrizal Basin, where the holotype was discovered.

facts.statement: Within the family Massospondylidae, Leyesaurus is most closely related to the genus Adeopapposaurus.
facts.quote: Within Massospondylidae, Leyesaurus was found to be most closely related to Adeopapposaurus.

facts.statement: Leyesaurus belongs to the family Massospondylidae.
Leyesaurus is classified within the class Saurischia.
Leyesaurus lived during the Hettangian to Toarcian stages, between 201.4 and 174.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Hettangian to Toarcian (201.4 to 174.7 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Leyesaurus is an extinct genus of massospondylid sauropodomorph dinosaur found in the San Juan Province of northwestern Argentina.
rejected.quote: Leyesaurus is an extinct genus of massospondylid sauropodomorph dinosaur known from the San Juan Province, northwestern Argentina.
